title: BPP and GDI based species delimitation
text:
BPP control files
Control files were created to run BPP analyses across a variety of models and prior distributions.

BPP A10 control files
The BPP analyses designated the A runs conduct a species delimitation analysis on a fixed species tree. The species tree used for the A10 runs is the TIP tree with each taxon as a separate branch (Z. japonicus, Z. meyeni, Z. montanus from the Northern Philippines, Z. montanus from the Southern Philippines and Indonesia, and Z. simplex, see above description of associated tree files). Below is the .ctl file for the first A series BPP run (A1). Several parameters on the control (.ctl) files are edited to execute different runs including the \(β_θ\) and \(β_τ\) parameters for the inverse 𝛤 prior distribution, and the species delimitation model (0 or 1). The \(β_θ\) and \(β_τ\) parameters for the inverse 𝛤 prior distribution are edited at the thetaprior and tauprior lines, each of which is specified by two digits for 𝛼 and 𝛽, but only the 𝛽 value will be changed across runs. A list of the .ctl files and the key parameters for each A series run are shown in the BPP A10 runs table in the A10 results section below. Note that beginning a line in the .ctl file with an asterisk causes BPP to ignore that line. Adding and deleting asterisks in front of particular lines of commands is a convenient way to add or delete particular parameters.
seed =  -1
seqfile = ZosteropsBPP_JMMSseq.txt
Imapfile = ZosteropsBPPtip_imap.txt
outfile = ZosteropsBPP_A10_RUNA1.out.txt
mcmcfile = ZosteropsBPP_A10_RUNA1.mcmc.txt

* speciesdelimitation = 0 # fixed species tree
* speciesdelimitation = 1 0 2    # speciesdelimitation algorithm0 and finetune(e)
speciesdelimitation = 1 1 2 1 # speciesdelimitation algorithm1 finetune (a m)
speciestree = 0 0.4 0.2 0.1   # speciestree pSlider ExpandRatio ShrinkRatio

* speciesmodelprior = 1  # 0: uniform LH; 1:uniform rooted trees; 2: uniformSLH; 3: uniformSRooted

species&tree = 5  Jp Me MoN MoS Si
                  93 10 6 25 14
                 ((((Jp, Me), MoN), MoS), Si);
phase = 0    # 0: phased sequences, 1: unphased diploid sequences, in newest version this command is called phase
usedata = 1    # 0: no data (prior); 1:seq like
nloci = 8    # number of data sets in seqfile
model = gtr
alphaprior = 1 1 4
cleandata = 1    # remove sites with ambiguity data (1:yes, 0:no)?

thetaprior = 3 0.01 e  # invgamma(a, b) for theta
tauprior = 3 0.002  # invgamma(a, b) for root tau & Dirichlet(a) for other tau's

locusrate = 1 0 0 1 iid   # (0: No variation, 1: estimate, 2: from file)
heredity = 2 ZosteropsBPP_heredity.txt   # (0: No variation, 1: estimate, 2: from file) & a_gamma b_gamma (if 1)
threads = 8
    
finetune = 1: 8 0.01 0.001 0.01 0.01  # auto (0 or 1): MCMC step lengths, last two values are for lrht and phi which in this run are not estimated so those numbers are excluded, if I wanted to add those estimates I would need two additional finetune values

print = 1 1 0 0   # MCMC samples, locusrate, heredityscalars Genetrees
burnin = 10000
sampfreq = 2
nsample = 100000


BPP A00 control files
The BPP analyses designated the B, C, D, and E runs conduct a species delimitation analysis on a fixed species tree. For the B runs the \(β_θ\) and \(β_τ\) parameters for the inverse 𝛤 prior distribution are 0.001 and 0.004 respectively. For the C runs the \(β_θ\) and \(β_τ\) parameters are 0.002 and 0.004, for the D runs these values are 0.001 and 0.0005, and for the E runs these values are 0.002 and 0.0005. Running BPP independently for different, but reasonable, distributions of 𝜃 and 𝜏 is used to assess the sensitivity of our estimates of these parameters to the priors. Note that for all the A00 runs (run series B-E) the speciesdelimitation selections are omitted by being preceded by an asterisk, as is the speciesmodelprior selection. Three replicate runs are done for each combination of 𝜃 and 𝜏 priors and each species tree (TIP, MID1, MID2, and ROOT, see above). Starting each .ctl file with seed = -1 creates a different random number seed for each replicate run. Independent runs for each species tree will be used to estimate 𝜃 and 𝜏 which will in turn be used to estimate the genealogical diversity index (GDI) for each branch (see description of GDI below). Below is an example of a B run control file. A list of the .ctl files and the key parameters for each set of runs in the B-E series run are shown in the BPP A00 runs table in the A00 results section below.
seed =  -1
seqfile = ZosteropsBPP_JMMSseq.txt
Imapfile = ZosteropsBPPtip_imap.txt
outfile = ZosteropsBPP_A00_RUNB1.out.txt
mcmcfile = ZosteropsBPP_A00_RUNB1.mcmc.txt

speciesdelimitation = 0 # fixed species tree
* speciesdelimitation = 1 0 2    # speciesdelimitation algorithm0 and finetune(e)
* speciesdelimitation = 1 1 2 1 # speciesdelimitation algorithm1 finetune (a m)
speciestree = 0 0.4 0.2 0.1   # speciestree pSlider ExpandRatio ShrinkRatio

* speciesmodelprior = 1  # 0: uniform LH; 1:uniform rooted trees; 2: uniformSLH; 3: uniformSRooted

species&tree = 5  Jp Me MoN MoS Si
                  93 10 6 25 14
                 ((((Jp, Me), MoN), MoS), Si);
phase = 0    # 0: phased sequences, 1: unphased diploid sequences, in newest version this command is called phase
usedata = 1    # 0: no data (prior); 1:seq like
nloci = 8    # number of data sets in seqfile
model = gtr
alphaprior = 1 1 4
cleandata = 1    # remove sites with ambiguity data (1:yes, 0:no)?

thetaprior = 3 0.001 e  # invgamma(a, b) for theta
tauprior = 3 0.004  # invgamma(a, b) for root tau & Dirichlet(a) for other tau's

locusrate = 1 0 0 1 iid   # (0: No variation, 1: estimate, 2: from file)
heredity = 2 ZosteropsBPP_heredity.txt   # (0: No variation, 1: estimate, 2: from file) & a_gamma b_gamma (if 1)
threads = 8
    
finetune = 1: 8 0.01 0.001 0.01 0.01  # auto (0 or 1): MCMC step lengths, last two values are for lrht and phi which in this run are not estimated so those numbers are excluded, if I wanted to add those estimates I would need two additional finetune values

print = 1 1 0 0   # MCMC samples, locusrate, heredityscalars Genetrees
burnin = 10000
sampfreq = 2
nsample = 100000

title: BPP and GDI based species delimitation
text:
Running BPP
Upon installing BPP v4.7.0 a directory will be created containing a bin folder with the BPP application (on Mac OS that directory is bpp-4.7.0-macos-aarch64). To execute a BPP run copy the following needed files to this directory (in this example we will be running the B1 run, an A00 analysis with .ctl file ZosteropsA00_RUNB1.bpp.ctl).

ZosteropsA00_RUNB1.bpp.ctl
ZosteropsBPP_JMMSseq.txt
ZosteropsBPP_heredity.txt
ZosteropsBPPtip_imap.txt

The only files that change between runs is the .ctl file and the imap file.
Navigate to the BPP directory with the bin folder containing the bpp program. In the terminal run the following command (make sure the needed files are in the working directory).
bin/bpp --cfile ZosteropsA00_RUNB1.bpp.ctl
Upon completion multiple files will be generated by this analysis.

FigTree.tre This is a tree file generated with 𝜃 as node labels and 𝜏 and 95% highest posterior density (HPD) for 𝜏 as branch lengths based on the tree topology given in the analysis.
Eight .sample.txt files one for each locus in the sequence file (locus.[1-8].sample.txt).
SeedUsed A text file recording the random number seed used for the run.
ZosteropsBPP_A00_RUNB1.mcmc.txt A text file containing the results from the MCMC chain.
ZosteropsBPP_A00_RUNB1.out.txt A text file summarizing the output of the run (for A10 runs this will include whether the analysis supported a split at each node along with the posterior probability of a split). For each run the name of the .mcmc and .out files will be specified by the .ctl file.

Repeat this process for each .ctl file and for the A00 runs replicate each run three times. Once each run is complete copy and organize the results to an appropriate directory.

A10 species delimitation results
In the A10 species delimitation analysis BPP returns a posterior probability for each node in the species tree provided, for this analysis the TIP tree in the file ZosteropsBPPtip_imap.txt. A result of 1 indicates a split at that node was supported and a 0 indicates that a lump was supported for the branches at that node. For all the A10 runs listed in the BPP A10 runs table above a split was supported at every node (1111, see tree below) with a posterior probability of 1.0.

# A RUNS are BPP runs under the A10 conditions with species delimitation under a fixed tree.
# B-E RUNS are BPP runs under the A00 conditions with no species delimitation and a fixed tree.
# Each set of runs are done under three replicates, four imap files corresponding to different branches of the tree (tip, mid1, mid2, root), and four different combinations of theta and tau prior distributions.
# Taxon codes for trees: Jp (Z. japonicus), Me (Z. meyeni), MoN (Northern Philippine Z. montanus on Luzon and Mindoror), MoS (Southern Philippine Z. montanus in the Visayas and Mindanao), Si (outgroup, Z. simplex on Mainland Asia and Taiwan)
# Trees for .ctl files...
  # B RUNS Tip ((((Jp, Me), MoN), MoS), Si)
  # C RUNS Mid1 (((JpMe, MoN), MoS), Si)
  # D RUNS Mid2 ((JpMeMoN, MoS), Si)
  # E RUNS Root (JpMeMoNMoS, Si)
# Beta values for Theta and Tau...
  # Z1 0.001 0.004  Z2 0.002 0.004  Z3 0.001 0.000  Z4 0.002 0.0005
  # Tip B1-3 0.001 0.004 B4-6 0.002 0.004 B7-9 0.001 0.0005 B10-12 0.002 0.0005

Pairwise Fst heatmap
Create a heatmap of the pairwise Fst measurements for each combination of taxa/populations.

ggplot(data = ZosteropsFSTheat, aes(x = X1, y = X2, fill = value))+
  geom_tile()+
  geom_text(data = ZosteropsFSTheat, aes(label = round(value, 2)))+
  theme_minimal()+
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "white", high = "red", space = "Lab", name = "Fst")+

Create a heatmap of the pairwise Fst measurements for each combination of taxa/populations but this time reorganize so that populations within the same taxon are kept together and they are ordered from high similarity to low similarity.

# Define the desired order for the axes
ZosteropsFST_reorder <- c("japonicusJAPAN", "japonicusKOREA", "japonicusRYUKYUn", "japonicusRYUKYUc", "japonicusRYUKYUs", "japonicusIZU", "japonicusOGASAWARA", "japonicusHAWAII", "meyeniLANYU", "meyeniBATAN", "montanusNORTH", "montanusPALAWAN", "montanusVISAYAS", "montanusMINDANAO", "montanusINDONESIA", "simplexASIA", "simplexNA", "erythropleurus", "everetti", "nigrorum", "palpebrosus")
# Convert the factors in the data to match the desired order
ZosteropsFSTheatRO <- ZosteropsFSTheat
ZosteropsFSTheatRO$X1 <- factor(ZosteropsFSTheat$X1, levels = ZosteropsFST_reorder)
ZosteropsFSTheatRO$X2 <- factor(ZosteropsFSTheat$X2, levels = ZosteropsFST_reorder)
# Create the heatmap with ggplot
library(ggplot2)
ggplot(data = ZosteropsFSTheatRO, aes(x = X1, y = X2, fill = value)) +
  geom_tile() +  
  geom_text(aes(label = round(value, 2))) +  
  theme_minimal() +  
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "white", high = "red", space = "Lab", name = "Fst") + 
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1), axis.text.y = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

title: Linear morphometrics
text:
Goals
Included here is are analyses of morphological phenotypes in East Asian Zosterops taken from linear measurements of museum skins at the Cincinnati Museum Center, National Museum of Natural History at the Smithsonian, and the American Museum of Natural History.

title: Linear morphometrics
text:
Getting started
We are using R version 4.4.2, RStudio version 2024.09.1 for the analysis. Quarto version 1.6.39 for Mac OS was used to document the workflow. Set the working directory in RStudio to one where the Zosterops skins linear measurements.csv data file is accessible.

Packages
Set the working directory to one where the file Zosterops_linear_measurements.csv is accessible. Install the following packages.

ggplot2 (Wickham 2016)
dplyr (Wickham et al. 2023)
tidyr (Wickham, Vaughan, and Girlich 2024)
gt (Iannone et al. 2024)
factoextra (Kassambara and Mundt 2020)
broom (Robinson, Hayes, and Couch 2024)
readr (Wickham, Hester, and Bryan 2024)
gridExtra (Auguie 2017)

Load the package libraries.

Data files
Morphological data for this analysis is in the comma delimited file titled Zosterops_linear_measurements.csv. Import the morphological dataset using read.csv and summarize. In total 214 individual specimens were measured and recorded across three museum collections (Cincinnati Museum Center, The American Museum of Natural History, and the National Museum of Natural history at the Smithsonian). Measurements for 180 skins were retained for analysis after omitting those cases where there was some ambiguity regarding the taxon designation or locality or where damaged or poorly positioned specimens created missing measurements.

# Import data from CSV file
ZosteropsMorph <- read.csv('./Data/Morphometrics/Zosterops_linear_measurements.csv')

title: Linear morphometrics
text:
Principal component analyses (PCA)

PCA for species

# Group data by 'species' and select relevant variables for PCA
ZosteropsMorph_species <- ZosteropsMorph %>%
  select(species, BillCulmen, BillNareTip, BillDepth, BillWidth, Tarsus, Wing, Tail) %>%
  group_by(species)

# Perform PCA on the selected variables
pca_result <- prcomp(ZosteropsMorph_species[, -1], center = TRUE, scale. = TRUE)

# Convert PCA result to a data frame for plotting
pca_data <- as.data.frame(pca_result$x)

# Add 'species' variable to PCA data for coloring
pca_data$species <- ZosteropsMorph_species$species

# Plot the first two principal components
ggplot(pca_data, aes(x = PC1, y = PC2, color = species)) +
  geom_point(size = 3) + 
  labs(title = "PCA of Zosterops Morphological Measurements",
       x = "Principal Component 1",
       y = "Principal Component 2") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.title = element_blank())










PCA for subspecies

# Group data by 'Name' (subspecies) and select relevant variables for PCA
ZosteropsMorph_subspecies <- ZosteropsMorph %>%
  select(Name, BillCulmen, BillNareTip, BillDepth, BillWidth, Tarsus, Wing, Tail) %>%
  group_by(Name)

# Perform PCA on the selected variables
pca_result <- prcomp(ZosteropsMorph_subspecies[, -1], center = TRUE, scale. = TRUE)

# Convert PCA result to a data frame for plotting
pca_data <- as.data.frame(pca_result$x)

# Add 'Name' variable to PCA data for coloring
pca_data$Name <- ZosteropsMorph_subspecies$Name

# Plot the first two principal components
ggplot(pca_data, aes(x = PC1, y = PC2, color = Name)) +
  geom_point(size = 3) + 
  labs(title = "PCA of Zosterops Morphological Measurements",
       x = "Principal Component 1",
       y = "Principal Component 2") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.title = element_blank())

title: Linear morphometrics
text:
Box-and-whisker plots and pairwise t-tests

Species plots, summaries, and t-tests
Define color values for box plots to match prior color schemes.

species_colors <- c("#004949", "#DB6D00", "#D82632", "#FED439", "#FA9C88", "#924900", "#008600")

Create box-and-whisker plots for each individual trait.

# Define a function to create boxplots for each trait
create_boxplot <- function(ZosteropsMorph_species, trait) {
  ggplot(ZosteropsMorph_species, aes_string(x = "species", y = trait)) + 
    geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) + # Boxplot without outliers
    geom_jitter(width = 0.2, aes(color = species), size = 2, alpha = 0.5) + # Add jitter for individual points
    labs(title = paste("Boxplot of", trait, "by Species"), x = "Species", y = trait) + 
    scale_color_manual(values = species_colors) +
    theme_minimal() # Minimal theme for better aesthetics

# Conduct pairwise statistical tests between every pair of species for specified variables
results_list_species <- list() # Initialize a list to store results
# Loop through each trait for pairwise tests
for (trait in traits) {
  # Perform pairwise t-tests
  pairwise_results_species <- pairwise.t.test(ZosteropsMorph_species[[trait]], 
                                       ZosteropsMorph_species$species, 
                                       p.adjust.method = "bonferroni")
  
  # Convert results to a tidy format
  tidy_results_species <- tidy(pairwise_results_species) %>%
    mutate(p.value = format.pval(p.value, digits = 2, format = "e")) # Format p-values in scientific notation
  
  results_list_species[[trait]] <- tidy_results_species # Store results in the list
}

ZosteropsMorph_groups <- ZosteropsMorph %>%

# Define a function to create boxplots for each trait
create_boxplot <- function(data, trait) {
  ggplot(data, aes_string(x = "Group", y = trait)) +
    geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) + # Boxplot without outliers
    geom_jitter(width = 0.2, aes(color = Group), size = 2, alpha = 0.5) + # Add jitter for individual points
    scale_color_manual(values = group_colors) + # Define colors for groups
    theme_minimal() + # Minimal theme for better aesthetics
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)) # Adjust labels on X axis
}

# Conduct pairwise statistical tests between every pair of species for specified variables
results_list_groups <- list() # Initialize a list to store results
# Loop through each trait for pairwise tests
for (trait in traits) {
  # Perform pairwise t-tests
  pairwise_results_groups <- pairwise.t.test(ZosteropsMorph_groups[[trait]], 
                                       ZosteropsMorph_groups$Group, 
                                       p.adjust.method = "bonferroni")
  
  # Convert results to a tidy format
  tidy_results_groups <- tidy(pairwise_results_groups) %>%
    mutate(p.value = format.pval(p.value, digits = 2, format = "e")) # Format p-values in scientific notation
  
  results_list_groups[[trait]] <- tidy_results_groups # Store results in the list
}
# Combine all results into a single data frame
final_results_groups <- bind_rows(results_list_groups, .id = "trait")
# Save the results to a CSV file
write.csv(final_results_groups, "pairwise_test_results_groups.csv", row.names = FALSE)

# Define the traits to create tables for
traits <- c('BillCulmen', 'BillNareTip', 'BillDepth', 'BillWidth', 'Tarsus', 'Wing', 'Tail')
# Loop through each trait to create and save tables
for (trait in traits) {
  # Filter data for the current trait
  trait_data_groups <- data %>% filter(trait == !!trait)
  
  # Create a readable table for the current trait
  table_name_groups <- paste0(trait, "_results_groups.csv")
  write_csv(trait_data_groups, table_name_groups)
